items.title: The Invisible Guest
items.reason: The apparently impossible locked-room killing and an earlier concealed hit-and-run remain central throughout the film. The attorney's interrogation systematically tests Adrián's inconsistent accounts, exposing fresh clues and producing multiple versions of the same events; the audience repeatedly revises who lied, who killed whom and why. Substantive whole-film criticism describes an unusually high cadence of revelations and reversals, strong suspense, visual polish and a coherent final explanation. Limitations: the story's impossibility is a staged crime, not a supernatural or physical anomaly; some solutions depend on highly engineered coincidences, and the affair/relationship is a motive rather than the primary genre. Investigation is active but distinct from the more frequent explanatory reframing.

items.title: The Body
items.reason: A missing corpse, a panicked morgue guard, contradictory clues and the suspicion that the supposedly dead woman is orchestrating events create a sustained why/how mystery. Inspector Peña's inquiries and Álex's increasingly desperate attempts to interpret evidence continue through the morgue-set night; the drug TH-16, the lover's disputed identity and the detective's past all receive concrete explanations in the finale. Whole-film reviews describe maintained tension, red herrings and a powerful final reversal. Weaknesses: the cycle of ominous clue, attempted cover-up and confrontation becomes repetitive around the middle; much of the largest reframing arrives late, not in a continuous chain; some plotting strains plausibility and the camerawork is less distinctive. The apparently uncanny occurrences ultimately have a human explanation rather than a supernatural one.
